
An experiment is a set of conditions: one model at different initial values, doses or parameters.
[`solveODEBatch()`](../reference/solveODEBatch.html) solves all conditions of one model in one
`.Call`, on OpenMP threads with dynamic scheduling and without the R API inside the parallel
region. The results equal those of a serial `solveODE()` loop bit for bit, for any thread count.

```{r library}
library(cppDE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Model definition

The decay chain, with forward sensitivities and in reverse mode, compiled into one shared object.

```{r models}
eqns  <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")
parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)
times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)

chain  <- cppODE(eqns, modelname = "g6_chain", compile = FALSE)
chainR <- cppODE(eqns, derivMode = "reverse", modelname = "g6_chainR", compile = FALSE)
compile(chain, chainR, output = "guide6", cores = 2)
```

## Solving a batch

`conditions` is a list of argument lists, one per condition. An element of a condition overrides
the batch-wide argument of the same name: `times`, `parms`, `tangent`, `hessian`, `cotangent`,
`curvature`, `fixed`, `forcings`, the tolerances and step limits, `keepStore`, `store`,
`sensErrCon`, `adjoint`, `maxOrder` and `stald`, each as in
[`solveODE()`](../reference/solveODE.html). Here three initial amounts of $A$, the last on a longer
grid.

```{r batch}
conditions <- list(
  low  = list(parms = c(A = 0.5, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)),
  mid  = list(parms = c(A = 1,   B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)),
  high = list(parms = c(A = 2,   B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2), times = seq(0, 20, by = 0.2)))

batch <- solveODEBatch(chain, conditions, times = times, cores = 2)
names(batch)
attr(batch, "threads")
```

Each element is a `solveODE()` result.

```{r batch-plot, fig.height = 3}
long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(batch), function(cn)
  cbind(longFormat(batch[[cn]], "B", sens = FALSE), condition = cn)))
long$condition <- factor(long$condition, c("low", "mid", "high"))

ggplot(long, aes(time, value, color = condition)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(y = "B", color = "initial A")
```

```{r batch-serial}
serial <- lapply(conditions, function(cond)
  solveODE(chain, if (is.null(cond$times)) times else cond$times, cond$parms))
identical(lapply(batch, `[[`, "tangent"), lapply(serial, `[[`, "tangent"))
```

`fixed` restricts the sensitivities per call, without recompiling.

```{r batch-fixed}
dimnames(solveODEBatch(chain, conditions, times = times, fixed = c("A", "B"))$low$tangent)[[3]]
```

## Failed conditions

All conditions run, then `onFailure` decides: `"stop"` (default) raises one error naming the
failed conditions, `"warn"` and `"silent"` return the partial results. `$diagnostics` holds the
return code of each condition.

```{r failure}
limited <- list(ok  = list(parms = parms),
                bad = list(parms = c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 1e8, k2 = 0.2), maxsteps = 10))
res <- solveODEBatch(chain, limited, times = times, onFailure = "warn")
sapply(res, function(r) r$diagnostics$return_code)
res$bad$diagnostics$message
```

`traceFile` writes the step trace of each condition, for a model built with `stepTrace = TRUE`.

## Threads and BLAS

`cores` sets the thread count. The default is the first of `getOption("cppDE.cores")`,
`getOption("Ncpus")` and the number of physical cores that is set; `cores = 1` forces the serial
loop.

| Threads | Value |
|:--|:--|
| default | `cores`, capped at the processor count, also for fewer conditions (the team persists between calls) |
| single condition, enclosing OpenMP region, `fork()` child | one |
| BLAS during a batch | one |
| BLAS and OpenMP across `fork()` | one in the child, restored in the parent |

Table: Thread counts of a batch.

`attr(, "threads")` reports the count used. [`batchAvailable()`](../reference/batchAvailable.html)
reports whether a model solves batches in parallel: the batch entry point, OpenMP in cppDE and
OpenMP in the shared object of the model. [`forkGuard()`](../reference/forkGuard.html) reports the
BLAS whose thread count cppDE steers, so that a threaded BLAS does not deadlock in a child of
`parallel::mclapply()`.

```{r threads}
unlist(batchAvailable(chain))
str(forkGuard())
```

## Prepared batches

[`prepareBatch()`](../reference/prepareBatch.html) validates and converts the conditions once.
[`solveBatch()`](../reference/solveBatch.html) then takes new numbers per condition, matched by
position: `parms`, `tangent`, `hessian`, `cotangent`, `curvature`, `adjoint` and `store`, each a
list with one element per condition and of the prepared shape. Times, tolerances and every other
argument need a new `prepareBatch()`, here also the grid of the third condition.

A fit of $k_1$ and $k_2$, shared by the three conditions, to noisy readings of $B$:

```{r prepared-data}
set.seed(2)
tdata <- 0:10
data  <- lapply(batch, function(r)
  r$variable[match(tdata, r$time), "B"] + rnorm(length(tdata), sd = 0.01))
x0    <- lapply(conditions, function(cond) cond$parms[c("A", "B")])

h <- prepareBatch(chain, lapply(conditions, `[`, "parms"), times = tdata)

objective <- function(k) {
  sol <- solveBatch(h, parms = lapply(x0, c, k), cores = 2)
  res <- Map(function(r, d) r$variable[, "B"] - d, sol, data)
  grad <- Reduce(`+`, Map(function(r, e) 2 * colSums(e * r$tangent[, "B", names(k)]), sol, res))
  structure(sum(unlist(res)^2), gradient = grad)
}
fit <- optim(c(k1 = 1, k2 = 0.1), function(k) objective(k),
             function(k) attr(objective(k), "gradient"), method = "BFGS")
fit$par
fit$convergence
```

## Reverse mode in a batch

A reverse-mode model takes one cotangent per condition. With `keepStore = TRUE` the forward passes
keep their checkpoints; a prepared batch then runs the backward sweeps alone, from the stores and
new cotangents. The gradient of the objective at the start values of the fit, from the residuals
as cotangents:

```{r reverse}
k0    <- c(k1 = 1, k2 = 0.1)
atK0  <- lapply(x0, function(x) list(parms = c(x, k0)))
fwd   <- solveODEBatch(chainR, lapply(atK0, c, keepStore = TRUE), times = tdata)

cotangent <- Map(function(r, d) cbind(A = 0, B = 2 * (r$variable[, "B"] - d)), fwd, data)
hr <- prepareBatch(chainR, atK0, times = tdata, cotangent = cotangent[[1]])
sweep <- solveBatch(hr, cotangent = cotangent, store = lapply(fwd, `[[`, "store"))

Reduce(`+`, lapply(sweep, function(r) r$cotangent[c("k1", "k2"), 1]))
attr(objective(k0), "gradient")
```

The two agree to the integration tolerance; [4. Reverse mode](guide-reverse.html) describes stores
and cotangents. Models from [`cvode()`](guide-cvode.html) have the same batch entry.
